title: A ready PR does not wait behind unrelated PRs in the queue
why:
[18:10 CST Nov 15, triage] Owner words, typed 18:10 CST per the consultant (relayed, verbatim): "yes merge 3545 now. in general things shouldnt have had to wait for other stuff behind to merge imagine sand shifting through multiple strainers in a sense man cmon we’ve talked abt this". Rulings own-ready-pr-no-queue-wait (standing, "in general") and own-merge-3545-now (the one merge). The gate it touches: session-tiers.md Batch runner, "It still marks ready only while no job is queued". Neighbours: ruling own-ready-by-priority, debt draft stale-merge-ref-ready-red. (source: coordinator and consultant 18:11 CST, relayed by triage; not read by triage as typed)

[18:39 CST Nov 15, triage] Owner picked 902 b (ruling own-ready-gate-unrelated-prs, from the page's save comment 18:37 CST): overturn the ready gate only for PRs that touch different areas. Runner 10's proposed definition (its own, not owner-checked), 18:39 CST: an area is a top-level folder a PR's changed files sit in (docs, hooks, merge, skills, tests, lint, root); two PRs are unrelated when their folder sets share no folder. First sample, REST file lists at 18:39 for five PRs: #3522 docs+merge; #3545 merge; #3535 root+docs+hooks+merge+tests; #3474 docs+hooks+merge+tests; #3514 docs+skills. Only #3514 vs #3545 is unrelated: 1 of 10 pairs, so the folder rule barely changes the queue. A tighter definition (no shared file, no test naming the other's file) is not measured; runner 10 was asked to measure it. n=1 sample of five; no outcome (conflict or red main) counted. Also: the owner's "B for sure" merge-on-lint-pass (#3562) is a separate rule that removes the CI wait. (source: runner 10 18:39 CST via the coordinator, relayed by triage; runner 10's own proposal, not owner-checked)
